root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `fnv_32a_buf()` may enter its fallthrough hashing body, it must establish `len > 0`. A zero-length family string must return the running hash unchanged instead of executing any `*bp++` dereference.
root_cause_criterion.description: The missing source guard is the zero-length check at the `fnv_32a_buf()` entry. The vulnerable original reaches the protected `case 2` read with `len_arg=0`, while the fixed original is guarded on the stock PoC and the closest source-grounded witness `font_tag_at_AB` executes the same protected event cleanly with `len_arg=2`.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original violates the required predicate (`len_arg=0`) and still reaches `hash_case2_sink`. The fixed original is guarded because it records the same root event but no sink event. The adjacent witness `font_tag_at_AB` satisfies the predicate (`len_arg=2`) and genuinely executes `hash_case2_sink` on the fixed side.

nodes.state: At the sanitizer sink on `case 2`, the current hash cursor `bp` is already beyond the original `buf` base, so the fallthrough dereference executes after prior reads have advanced into the logically empty input.
When `update_font()` strips the leading vertical-font marker `@`, it leaves `desc.family.len == 0`; that empty family string is the source-level value later passed into `fnv_32a_buf()`.

edges.relation: The same `len` checked by the missing zero-length guard remains unchanged when execution reaches the `case 2` sink, so the sink runs with the exact zero-length input that should have been rejected.
The empty family length produced by `update_font()` is passed unchanged through font-cache hashing into `fnv_32a_buf()` as its `len` argument.
